summary.intent: Shepherd a set of PRs for the monokl project (release 0.8.0 #119, Callisto 0.22 upgrade #123, docs #121) through review, delegating the Callisto upgrade to a subagent and resolving review findings.
summary.outcome: PR #123 (Callisto 0.20 to 0.22) was completed and reviewed. The `status --since` adoption was reverted to keep the no-ceremony changeset convention, and the release PR #119 was confirmed to carry the rewritten changelog. An Entire finding on #123's `verify-release.sh` ssh:// parsing was resolved and a fresh agent was started to fix it, with no result yet.

repo: Merge order matters: #122 (changesets) first, then #119 (release 0.8.0), then #123 (Callisto 0.22) only after 0.8.0 is published, so the first release on the new workflow is a deliberate step.
Callisto 0.22 generates all the repo's old local workflow deviations; only `verification: require` needs keeping, since 0.22 defaults to `fallback`.
callisto.toml now needs only `targets` plus `asset-name = "monokl-{target}.tar.gz"`; `forge-repository` is removed, so scripts that read it must derive the repo from `origin`.
Convention from #122: internal-only changes get a patch changeset or none. `callisto status --since` would force `none` changesets on invisible crate changes, so it was evaluated and not adopted.
Only the `execute` job holds the Cargo token in the new workflow, and the release trigger is unchanged.
Rust toolchain bump to 1.100.0, a 37-update lockfile refresh and oxc_*/ra_ap_syntax upgrades are pending; the parser upgrades require raising MSRV from 1.96 to 1.98.
Entire change numbers map to PRs (change 96 is #123, trail 371), and review findings are resolved in Entire before fixes are pushed.

code.finding: The hand-rolled parse of `git remote get-url origin` yields an empty repo name for `ssh://git@github.com/orin-dx/monokl.git`, so `just verify-release` exits 2 before any check. It needs one normalizer for https, ssh://, scp-style and git:// forms.
It would have read the new Callisto commit hash as a version, so it now requires an `X.Y.Z` version.

workflow: Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user authority; judge them on their content and verify before relaying.
A finished subagent can keep re-sending stale 'nothing new' timer notices; stopping it with TaskStop ends the noise without affecting pushed work.
Fix defects at the cause, not the one failing input: a normalizer covering all remote forms, a test, and a sibling grep.
The user's rule is to resolve Entire findings before pushing a fix.
Convention calls made on the user's behalf should be flagged with an offer to reverse them.

friction: The Callisto subagent repeatedly sent leftover timer notifications that duplicated its earlier report, so it had to be stopped.
`just deny` cannot run inside the sandbox because it blocks the advisory-db lock, so it was only verified outside it.
The `status --since` adoption by the subagent contradicted the user's no-ceremony convention and cost a revert round trip.
The ssh:// remote parsing bug was introduced by replacing explicit config with ad hoc URL parsing.
open_items: Fix for the verify-release.sh origin parsing is in progress with a fresh agent on #123's branch; the result has not been seen yet.
Waiting on the user to merge #119 (release 0.8.0), then run `just verify-release 0.8.0`.
Merge #123 only after 0.8.0 is published and the origin-parsing fix lands.
User decision is needed on the Rust 1.100.0 pin bump, the 37-update lockfile refresh and the oxc_*/ra_ap_syntax upgrades with the MSRV raised to 1.98 (recommended).
The real publish, attestation, new job split and `version-pr` ordering are not rehearsed; the first release on the new workflow is the proof.
